0086.name: Slippery level flag
desc: Nonzero on a slippery (ice) level, 0 otherwise. Mario's ground physics and walk animation take a different path
when it is set, and skid smoke is only spawned when it is 0. Bit 7 is set at level start by ROR when tileset-related
value $192A is 5. Read by the Mario ground speed, jump start and shelless Koopa routines.
Values: 0 = normal ground; nonzero = slippery.

0088.name: Mario animation timer
desc: Per-animation countdown or index for Mario's scripted animations. Pipe entry/exit (animations 5, 6, 7) set it to the
pipe timer and count it down by one per frame; the scripted walk (A) uses it as the offset into the input script; the
cutscene movement (C) uses it as the frames left for the current command. Level start sets it to the Mario Start! timer.
Set by the pipe-entry collision code ($F40A) and read by the Mario animation routines. Also hit by pointer tables.

0089.name: Mario animation scratch
desc: Second per-animation byte next to $0088. Pipe entry stores the pipe direction index here and the pipe animations read it;
the scripted walk (animation A) counts the frames remaining in the current script step down in it; level start sets it to 1.

008A.name: General scratch / pointer low
desc: Reused by many unrelated routines. As a 24-bit source pointer $008A/$008B/$008C it is the stream read by the GFX
decompression and ending palette code (byte read through it, bank in $008C). Also a menu checksum sum, file select value,
a pass counter for overworld tile edits, and the saved Mario Y speed while climbing.
In Mario collision it is the water contact bits (cleared at the start); bit 0 is set for touching certain tiles.

008B.name: General scratch / tile flags
desc: Reused scratch. As the middle byte of the pointer $008A/$008B/$008C it is the high byte of the GFX decompression source.
In Mario's climbing code it holds the climbable-tile contact flags: Mario animation 0 sets it to $1F when touching all
climbable tiles, the climb routine reads it, and level collision clears it. The overworld border icon drawer uses it as
a Y offset (walking poses are drawn 5 pixels higher).

008C.name: General scratch / bank byte
desc: Reused scratch. As the third byte of the pointer $008A/$008B/$008C it is the bank byte of the GFX decompression source,
incremented when the pointer wraps past $FFFF. The overworld sprite drawers use it as a tile counter (3 for a 2x2 sprite,
7 for the 8 tiles of Mario riding Yoshi). Block interaction copies Mario's $0093 into it.

008D.name: General scratch / loop counter
desc: Reused scratch. The ending palette and GFX decompression code counts it down by 2 per step as a loop counter; level
collision stores a saved copy of the tile-contact flag ([$13EF]) in it, which the block and slope collision then reads.

008E.name: Scratch: layer 2 orientation bits
desc: Reused scratch. Mario level collision stores [$5B] & $82 here (the level orientation bits for layer 2); the block and
slope collision clears it to 0; the pipe-entry lookup and the Mode 7 boss room platform check also use it.

008F.name: Scratch: was-in-air flag
desc: Reused scratch. Level collision backs up the in-air flag RAM_IsFlying here before it is changed, so the block and slope
collision and the cape ground pound on landing can tell whether Mario was in the air. The ending decompression stores the
current command byte here, and the cutscene movement code uses it as the script position (+2 per command).

0090.name: Mario Y offset in block
desc: Y offset of Mario's collision point inside its 16x16 block; the block and slope collision uses it as an index when
looking up slope heights. Written and read in Mario's block and slope collision.

0091.name: Collision point Y offset
desc: Y offset of the collision point inside its block, computed by the block and slope collision as ($90 + table offset)
& $0F. Used right afterwards to compare against the slope height.

0092.name: Slope column X offset
desc: Column inside the block used for slope height lookups: (X offset + 8) & $0F, set in Mario's block and slope collision.
Also read by the cape ground pound on landing and by the pipe-entry map16 lookup.

0093.name: Block half flag
desc: 0 when Mario's collision point is in the left half of the 16x16 block, 1 for the right half (set by INC in the block and
slope collision). Block interaction reads it and copies it into $008C.

0094.name: Mario X position, low byte
desc: Mario's X position in pixels within the level; $0094 is the low byte and $0095 the high byte (screen number). It is
read by nearly every routine that needs Mario's location and written whenever Mario is moved: layer 2 displacement,
platforms and sprites carrying him, pipes, the keyhole, the level start position and wall pushes.
Read as a 16-bit word together with $0095.

0095.name: Mario X position, high byte
desc: High byte of Mario's X position ($0094 is the low byte): the screen number he is on. Platforms, carry sprites and Mega
Moles add sign extension and carry here when carrying Mario; the level loader sets it from the start position table.
Sprite spawners copy it as the X high of effects such as bubbles, splashes and smoke.

0096.name: Mario Y position, low byte
desc: Mario's Y position in pixels in the level; $0096 is the low byte and $0097 the high byte. Written by the level loader,
pipes, layer 2 displacement, platforms carrying him and cutscene movement; read by collision, sprite contact and effect
spawners. Level start sets it to $A0 for the intro.

0097.name: Mario Y position, high byte
desc: High byte of Mario's Y position ($0096 is the low byte). Set by the level loader from the start position table; bumped
by INC when Mario crosses into the next screen in the block collision; copied into spawned score sprites, bubbles, splashes
and fireballs. Set to 0 in the Mode 7 boss room.

0098.name: Block Y position, low
desc: Y position of the block being acted on: the 16x16 block hit by Mario, a sprite, the cape or a bounce sprite. Used to
generate or change a Map16 tile ($009C), spawn a bounce sprite or smoke, or look up a tile. Low byte; $0099 is the high.
Block interaction snaps it to the grid by clearing its low nibble.

0099.name: Block Y position, high
desc: High byte of the block Y position ($0098 is the low byte), i.e. the screen number for the block. Written by sprite and
extended sprite routines before a Map16 tile is generated or a bounce sprite is spawned.

009A.name: Block X position, low
desc: X position of the block being acted on, low byte ($009B is the high byte). Set from Mario, a sprite, the cape or an
extended sprite before calling the Map16 tile generation, bounce sprite spawn or smoke routines; block interaction snaps
it to the 16x16 grid. The bridge breaker mirrors it about the bridge center.

009B.name: Block X position, high
desc: High byte of the block X position ($009A is the low byte), i.e. the screen number. Set alongside $009A by the same
routines; also used as a Flat Palace Switch X high when the switch sprite is spawned.

009C.name: Block to generate
desc: Number of the block to generate at the position in $0098-$009B (the generate-tile handlers map it to a Map16 tile).
Set by the code that needs a block changed: $0D = used block, $02 = empty, $08 = Monty Mole hole, a growing pipe's tile.
Read by the Map16 tile generation routine.

009D.name: Sprites locked flag
desc: Freezes the sprites when nonzero: sprite main routines, many timers and extended sprites skip their update while it is
set. Set during power-up growth, Yoshi growing, pipe and other Mario animations; cleared (0) when the effect ends.
Read by almost every sprite routine.
Values: 0 = sprites run; nonzero = sprites frozen.

009E.name: Sprite number
009E.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: The sprite number (type) of each of the 12 sprite slots; it selects which main routine runs for the slot. Set when a
sprite spawns (e.g. from a block or the level) and rewritten when a sprite changes form (a Koopa becomes its shell).
Read by contact, interaction and physics routines to tell sprite types apart. Slot N is at $009E+N.

00A5.name: Sprite number, slot 7
desc: Entry for sprite slot 7 of the sprite number table at $009E. Extended sprite smoke, burst and fireball code loads it
and compares with $A9; the exact purpose is unclear (probably a special-sprite check).

00A6.name: Sprite number, slot 8
desc: Entry for sprite slot 8 of the sprite number table at $009E. The Bowser fight writes it to create a sprite in that
slot: $A1 (Mechakoopa) and $7C (Princess Peach) are set here.

00AA.name: Sprite Y speed
00AA.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Vertical speed of each sprite slot, signed (negative is up, positive is down), applied each frame by the sprite position
routines. Sprites set it to launch a jump ($D8 for Ludwig, $E3 for Blargg, $F8 rise for balloons), apply gravity by
incrementing it, or cap it at a terminal speed (e.g. $40 for Thwimp). Slot N is at $00AA+N.

00B5.name: Sprite Y speed, slot 11
00B5.kind: byte (entry of sprite Y speed table $00AA)
desc: Entry for sprite slot 11 of the table at $00AA. The only direct write is STA $B5,X in the extended sprite smoke puff
routine, where X is an extended sprite index, so the meaning there is something else (a value from a table indexed by
direction). Other hits are pointer table bytes.

00B6.name: Sprite X speed
00B6.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Horizontal speed of each sprite slot, signed (negative is left, positive is right), applied each frame by the sprite
position routines. Sprites set it to walk or jump (Ludwig jump speed, Koopa kicked speed), reverse it (Urchin, wall
hits), step it toward 0 (Boo, shelled Koopa sliding) or accelerate it. Slot N is at $00B6+N.
